final_answer.key_evidence_summary: Pod listing shows a single outlier: shippingservice-dcf97c8fd-lkfpz is 0/1 Running with 3 restarts (0s ago) while all other boutique pods are 1/1 with 0 restarts. Pod detail last_termination = Reason: Error, Exit Code: 2 (neither 137 OOMKilled nor 143 SIGTERM), ruling out a memory-limit kill. Pod events give the mechanism verbatim: 'Warning Unhealthy 3s (x9 over 83s) kubelet Liveness probe failed: Get "http://172.20.1.120:50051/": net/http: HTTP/1.x transport connection broken: malformed HTTP response "\x00\x00\x06\x04..."' followed by 'Normal Killing 3s (x3 over 63s) kubelet Container server failed liveness probe, will be restarted'. The \x00\x00\x06\x04 bytes are an HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame: shippingservice is a Go gRPC server, so an HTTP/1.x GET probe can never succeed. GetAppYAML confirms the defect inside one pod template: readinessProbe uses grpc port 50051 (correct) while livenessProbe uses httpGet path / port 50051 (wrong protocol). The Service port is literally named 'grpc' (port 50051 -> targetPort 50051) and env PORT=50051, so the port is correct and the protocol is wrong. GetAlerts returned no active metric anomalies (alerts are only a pointer, no object-layer support) and GetErrorLogs was empty, so the restart loop is caused by the liveness probe protocol mismatch, not by application code.
